Article Title: Florida confirms Burmese python breeding hotspot outside the Everglades, and wildlife experts fear it could be the start of a bigger spread
Article Text:
Florida confirms Burmese python population outside the Everglades

Why the snakes appeared there

How their feeding habits help them spread

What happens to native wildlife

Why most Burmese pythons go undetected

How Burmese pythons took hold in Florida

For years, efforts to track invasive Burmese pythons in Florida have centred on the Everglades, where the giant snakes have become one of the state's most persistent wildlife problems. That picture is beginning to change. Wildlife officials now say a separate breeding population has become established farther north along Florida's Gulf Coast, suggesting the species has gained another foothold beyond its long-recognised range. The discovery has renewed concerns among conservationists because isolated colonies can become difficult to contain once they begin reproducing. While Burmese pythons have already transformed parts of South Florida's ecosystems, scientists fear similar changes could gradually emerge in places that until recently were considered outside the snake's main stronghold.The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) has confirmed that Burmese pythons are now established in part of western Charlotte County. The area lies north of Naples and Fort Myers and represents a distinct population outside the species' long-recognised core range.For decades, established populations were largely associated with Everglades National Park before spreading across much of South Florida, stretching between Lake Okeechobee, Key Largo and western parts of Broward and Collier counties.The Charlotte County colony sits beyond that familiar distribution, making it a separate area of concern rather than simply another sighting. Officials began noticing a steady rise in reports from local communities several years ago. Sightings increased around Rotonda West, Placida, Englewood East and South Gulf Cove, prompting closer monitoring before biologists concluded that breeding animals were present."This is a generalist apex predator, and this is the why we're so interested in removing them from the ecosystem," Ian Bartoszek, a wildlife biologist and science coordinator at the Conservancy of Southwest Florida in Naples, as reported by ABC News.Wildlife specialists do not believe the Charlotte County population developed through a slow northward movement from existing Everglades populations. Instead, the available evidence points towards escaped or deliberately released captive snakes. Burmese pythons were widely imported into the United States through the exotic pet trade for decades, and accidental escapes as well as intentional releases have been linked to the species' establishment in Florida. Biologists studying the new colony say its characteristics match what they would expect from a satellite population created by human introduction rather than natural expansion across the landscape.Large Burmese pythons are capable of feeding on an unusually broad range of animals. Their diet includes raccoons, opossums, birds, bobcats and alligators, and they have even been documented consuming prey larger than many people would expect a snake to handle.That flexibility is one reason wildlife managers regard them as especially difficult to control. Rather than depending on a single food source, the snakes can shift between different prey as opportunities change, allowing them to survive in a variety of habitats.Conservation workers involved in python removal describe them as apex predators that can reshape local ecosystems once populations become established.The impact extends well beyond the loss of individual animals. Ecologists studying areas where pythons have been present for years have documented steep declines in many native mammal populations.As larger mammals disappear, ecosystems can gradually become less diverse. Scientists describe these altered environments as simplified systems where rodents and other invasive species may become relatively more common while many native animals become scarce.Researchers say this pattern has repeated itself across parts of South Florida, and preventing similar ecological changes elsewhere remains an ongoing challenge.Estimating the number of Burmese pythons living in Florida remains remarkably difficult.The snakes spend much of their time concealed in dense vegetation, wetlands and waterways, making them exceptionally hard to locate even during organised surveys. Research suggests that survey teams may detect only around one to three snakes for every hundred believed to be present within a search area.Even inside Everglades National Park, where specialist teams regularly search for pythons, finding one often requires many hours of fieldwork. That low detection rate means confirmed sightings probably represent only a small fraction of the animals actually living across the landscape.The Burmese python invasion has developed over several decades. Federal wildlife records indicate that roughly 180,000 of the snakes entered the United States between 1975 and 2018, largely through the pet trade.By around 2000, breeding populations had already become firmly established in South Florida. Since then, wildlife agencies have relied on public reports, organised removal programmes and scientific surveys in an attempt to slow their spread.Those efforts continue as officials monitor Charlotte and neighbouring Lee County for additional snakes. Detecting breeding groups early offers the best chance of limiting further expansion, although biologists acknowledge that managing an invasive predator of this size remains one of Florida's most demanding wildlife challenges.
Article Summary: Florida confirms Burmese python population outside the Everglades. Discovery has renewed concerns among conservationists. isolated colonies can become difficult to contain once they begin reproducing. Scientists fear similar changes could emerge in places that until recently were considered outside the snake's main stronghold.

Article Title: As temperatures soar, dozens of donkeys in UK are wearing pyjamas and 'don-gerees' to stop painful insect bites, and the clever reason is winning hearts
Article Text:
Why are the donkeys in the UK wearing pyjamas?



What are 'don-gerees'?





Why clothing works better than sprays

University donations support the project



About The Donkey Sanctuary

A simple idea with a big impact

As soaring summer temperatures bring swarms of biting insects across the UK, one animal charity in Devon has found an unexpectedly charming solution to keep its rescued donkeys comfortable. Around 40 donkeys at The Donkey Sanctuary in Sidmouth are now wearing adapted pyjama bottoms, leggings and specially designed "don-gerees" to shield their legs from painful fly bites. While the unusual outfits have attracted smiles online, they serve a serious purpose. The simple clothing hack helps prevent irritation, sores and skin infections caused by biting insects, while also giving unwanted clothes a useful second life and reducing textile waste.The clothing has been introduced to protect the donkeys during fly season, when biting insects are most active. Flies often target the animals' lower legs, causing painful bites that can lead to itching, open wounds and long-term skin problems.Older donkeys are particularly vulnerable because they may struggle more with repeated insect attacks and slower healing. Staff at the sanctuary wanted a practical, long-lasting way to improve their comfort throughout the warmer months.The idea evolved through trial and error. Caretakers initially experimented with socks to cover the donkeys' legs, but they repeatedly slipped off as the animals walked around their fields.They then tried adapting larger garments, including loose-fitting pyjama bottoms, maternity trousers and leggings. These stayed securely in place while allowing the donkeys to move naturally, making them a much more effective solution.Some of the customised outfits are affectionately called "don-gerees", a playful combination of the words donkey and dungarees.Each garment is carefully altered by staff to fit individual donkeys comfortably. The loose fabric moves gently as the animals walk, making it harder for flies to land and bite.Unlike insect repellents, which need to be applied repeatedly throughout the day, the adapted clothing provides continuous protection.The garments act as a physical barrier between the insects and the donkeys' skin while remaining lightweight enough for the animals to graze, walk and rest comfortably. Staff say the donkeys have adapted well to wearing their unusual outfits.The initiative is also helping reduce textile waste.The Donkey Sanctuary is encouraging people to donate unwanted loose-fitting clothing, including pyjama bottoms, maternity trousers and leggings. Garments in women's size 16 and above or men's large and above are especially useful because they can be adapted for the donkeys.Instead of ending up in landfill or being discarded, these clothes are transformed into protective wear that directly benefits rescued animals.The campaign recently received support from the University of St Andrews in Scotland.Through the university's Reuse Shop, students donated unwanted clothing that was no longer suitable for resale. Rather than being thrown away, the garments travelled more than 500 miles to Devon, where they were repurposed into protective clothing for the sanctuary's donkeys.Founded in 1969, The Donkey Sanctuary is an international animal welfare charity based near Sidmouth, Devon. It provides lifelong care for donkeys rescued from neglect, abuse and abandonment, while also supporting donkey welfare projects in countries around the world.The charity has cared for more than 11,000 donkeys over the years and continues to promote better welfare through veterinary care, education, research and rescue programmes.Although the sight of donkeys wearing pyjamas and "don-gerees" may seem amusing at first, the initiative reflects a thoughtful approach to animal welfare. By combining creativity with sustainability, the sanctuary has found a low-cost way to protect its animals from painful insect bites while reducing clothing waste. It is a reminder that sometimes the simplest ideas can make the biggest difference, both for the animals they protect and for the environment.
Article Summary: Around 40 donkeys at The Donkey Sanctuary in Sidmouth are now wearing adapted pyjama bottoms, leggings and specially designed "don-gerees" The clothing has been introduced to protect the donkeys during fly season. Flies often target the animals' lower legs, causing painful bites that can lead to itching and open wounds.

Article Title: The largest male great white shark ever tagged in the Atlantic has resurfaced after travelling 7,000 miles; scientists say his journey is far from over
Article Text:
The largest satellite-tagged male great white shark continues its Atlantic migration

A shark that has travelled thousands of miles

Why scientists keep watching

Why Deep Blue is still the biggest great white shark ever recorded

Tracking a species that still holds many mysteries

The Atlantic's largest satellite-tagged male great white shark has surfaced again near North Carolina's Outer Banks, offering marine scientists another glimpse into one of the ocean's most remarkable migrations. Known as Contender, the 14-foot, 1,700-pound shark briefly triggered its satellite tag after travelling more than 7,000 miles since being tagged in 2025. Although the transmission was too short to pinpoint his exact location, researchers believe he is continuing his annual journey towards northern feeding grounds.The latest detection also highlights how satellite tracking is helping scientists better understand the movements, habitats and long-term recovery of great white sharks, while putting Contender's impressive size into perspective alongside Deep Blue, the world's largest known great white shark.The latest update arrived when Contender's satellite tag briefly broke the water's surface, allowing it to communicate with orbiting satellites before disappearing beneath the sea again. The transmission lasted only moments, leaving scientists unable to determine the shark's precise location.Even so, the detection was enough to indicate that the animal is moving along the eastern coastline of the United States.Marine biologists following the project believe the shark is continuing the familiar northward journey that many adult great whites undertake as summer progresses.Adult white sharks do not remain in one place for long. As ocean temperatures shift through the seasons, they regularly travel between warmer southern waters and richer feeding grounds farther north.The waters around Cape Cod and Atlantic Canada become attractive destinations during late spring and summer because they provide abundant prey and conditions that suit the species. Grey seals, along with large shoals of fish, form an important part of the food available in these regions.Closer to the US northeast coast, white sharks are also known to feed on schools of menhaden gathering near shorelines, including areas around Long Island. Tracking individual sharks helps scientists understand how these seasonal movements connect different parts of the Atlantic ecosystem.Contender was fitted with a satellite tag during a research expedition off the coasts of Florida and Georgia in January 2025 as reported by The Sun. At the time, the mature male measured roughly 14 feet in length and weighed close to 1,700 pounds, making him the largest male white shark ever tagged by researchers working in the western North Atlantic.Since then, his recorded route has stretched for more than 7,000 miles. The shark has travelled between waters off Florida and the Gulf of St. Lawrence in Canada, reflecting the remarkable distances adult great whites routinely cover during their lives.The tracking device attached to Contender is expected to continue sending data for several years whenever it surfaces long enough to connect with satellites. Each successful transmission allows researchers to build a more detailed record of his movements.Satellite-tagged sharks provide information that would otherwise be almost impossible to collect. Their journeys reveal where mature animals spend different parts of the year, which habitats they rely on and how they respond to changing environmental conditions.Researchers also use these long-term records to improve understanding of breeding populations and recovery trends. Every new location contributes to a growing dataset that can support future conservation work and improve knowledge of one of the Atlantic's most closely studied marine predators.Although Contender is an exceptionally large male, he is not considered the biggest great white known to science.That distinction is widely associated with Deep Blue, a famous female great white estimated to measure around 20 feet in length and weigh roughly 4,500 pounds. Deep Blue has been photographed and filmed in waters near Hawaii and has become one of the most recognisable individual sharks ever recorded.The difference also reflects the species' biology. Female great white sharks typically grow considerably larger than males, sometimes reaching sizes that are rarely matched by their male counterparts.Great white sharks remain among the ocean's most wide-ranging predators, capable of travelling vast distances across entire coastlines and even between ocean basins. Despite decades of research, many aspects of their movements and behaviour are still being pieced together through satellite tracking projects.Contender's latest appearance near North Carolina adds another waypoint to a journey that is far from finished. Although the exact spot where he surfaced remains unknown, the brief signal suggests his seasonal migration is continuing much as scientists expected, offering another valuable insight into the life of one of the Atlantic's most impressive marine animals.
Article Summary: The 14-foot, 1,700-pound shark briefly triggered its satellite tag after travelling more than 7,000 miles since being tagged in 2025. Although the transmission was too short to pinpoint his exact location, researchers believe he is continuing his annual journey towards northern feeding grounds. Tracking individual sharks helps scientists understand how these seasonal movements connect different parts of the Atlantic.

Article Title: Who is Jelicia Westhoff? Maduka Okoye’s baby mama accuses Nigerian goalkeeper of cheating and abuse amid Cardi B rumours
Article Text:
Who is Jelicia Westhoff? Maduka Okoye’s baby mama accuses Nigerian goalkeeper of cheating and abuse amid Cardi B rumours (Image via Getty)

Jelicia Westhoff: Maduka Okoye’s longtime partner and mother of his son

Maduka Okoye faces fresh allegations after Cardi B dinner sighting

Jelicia Westhoff, the mother of Maduka Okoye’s son, is back in the headlines after posting serious allegations against the Nigerian goalkeeper on Instagram. Her posts came just hours after Okoye was seen having dinner with rapper Cardi B in Venice, Italy, leading many to connect the two events. Westhoff accused the Udinese goalkeeper of cheating, abuse and failing to care for their son. Okoye has not responded publicly to the claims, and neither he nor his representatives have issued a statement. The allegations have not been independently verified.Jelicia Westhoff is a Dutch model, entrepreneur and former beauty queen. She won the Miss Haarlem title in 2015 before moving into business. Along with her sisters, she co-founded the Westhoff Collection, a fashion brand based in Amsterdam. The family also runs businesses in children’s clothing, beauty products and makeup training.Westhoff and Maduka Okoye first met in 2020 and later welcomed their son, Emiliano Isaiah Okoye, on October 14, 2022. Over the years, she often shared family moments online and spoke about supporting Okoye during difficult periods in his football career. According to her earlier posts, she stood by him after surgery, encouraged him when he was struggling professionally and helped him through challenging times.Their relationship, however, has seen several public breakups and reconciliations.In September 2024, Westhoff announced they had split before later confirming they had worked things out. As recently as early July 2026, she suggested they were focused on family and moving forward together.The situation changed on July 20 after TMZ published videos showing Okoye having dinner with Cardi B at Gio’s restaurant inside the St. Regis hotel in Venice. The two had also attended the Jean Paul Gaultier Haute Couture show together during Paris Fashion Week earlier this month.Soon after those reports appeared, Westhoff shared a series of emotional Instagram Stories accusing Okoye of cheating and abuse. She wrote:“You was cheating on me with EVERYTHING, When I just gave birth to our baby, and i still choose to whipe your but because you just had an operation and NO one of your people looked out for you, because you wasnt even playing, YOU wasnt even on the couch you would cry your eyes out, i motivated you, cooked for you.”She later added:“INSTEAD OF loving US. YOU Beated me! Cheated ON ME. with MEN AND WOMAN YOUR a FU*KING DEMON WHO TRIED TO DESTROY MY LIFE. YOU DONT TAKE CARE OF YOUR 1 and only SON! BECAUSE I DONT WANT TO BE WITH YOU I WILL NEVER FORGIVE YOU.”Westhoff also claimed police had been called during previous incidents and said their son had been hospitalised several times in late 2025 while Okoye was absent. She shared screenshots that appeared to show legal communication about child support and parenting responsibilities.At the same time, she said her posts were not driven by jealousy over Cardi B and insisted she was speaking out because she no longer wanted to protect Okoye’s image.So far, Okoye has remained silent. Cardi B has also not commented on the dating rumours or Westhoff’s allegations.
Article Summary: Jelicia Westhoff is the mother of Maduka Okoye's son, Emiliano. She has accused the Udinese goalkeeper of cheating, abuse and failing to care for their son. Her posts came just hours after OkoyE was seen having dinner with rapper Cardi B in Venice, Italy, leading many to connect the two events.

Article Title: Mediators propose 10-day truce to revive interim deal: Iran official
Article Text: A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Monday that Tehran had received a proposal from mediators for a 10-day ceasefire in an effort to salvage the interim deal, intended to pave the way to a lasting agreement to end the war that began on Feb 28.Iran's foreign ministry said mediators had recently presented proposals to Tehran, signalling that diplomatic contacts remain active. Neither the ministry nor the official gave any further details.Separately, two Pakistani govt sources said Iran's interior minister Eskandar Momeni, on his second visit to Islamabad in less than a week, had asked Pakistan to resume its mediation role in Iran's conflict with the US.The diplomatic push followed another night of US strikes on Iranian cities and attacks by Iran's Revolutionary Guards on US military assets across the region. US President Trump defended the latest strikes on Iran as honouring the deaths of up to three American service members in recent Iranian attacks.The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), meanwhile, said two oil tankers had exploded after attempting to transit the strait via an "unsafe" route.On Sunday, the IRGC had said two ships were involved in an "accident" in the same area. It was unclear whether the two incidents were related.Separately, a vessel was struck by an unknown projectile off Oman's coast, overlooking the Strait of Hormuz, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said. The vessel remains adrift but the crew are safe, it said.US Central Command said its ninth consecutive night of strikes against Iran aimed at "degrading" the country's ability to attack commercial vessels in the strait. It gave no further details. In Iran, explosions were reported in Tabriz, Chabahar, Konarak, Bandar Mahshahr and Bandar Imam Khomeini. One person was killed and several others wounded southwest of Tabriz.
Article Summary: Iran's foreign ministry said mediators had recently presented proposals to Tehran, signalling that diplomatic contacts remain active. Two Pakistani govt sources said Iran's interior minister Eskandar Momeni had asked Pakistan to resume its mediation role in Iran's conflict with the US.

Article Title: Have demanded extradition of Hasina aide from India: Bangladesh minister
Article Text: DHAKA: Bangladesh said Monday a letter has been sent to India seeking the extradition of key Sheikh Hasina aide and former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal - who is said to have fled along with the former PM amid the "2024 uprising" against her govt.Asked if Dhaka would renew its extradition request for former PM Hasina, state minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaed Islam restricted her reply to reporters, saying, "Normally extradition request letters are sent separately, and they are sending letters for all individuals who remain fugitives.""Since he (Kamal) is a fugitive, we have given the letter that is required for his return. It has been sent recently, addressing only the former home minister," Islam said of Kamal who was sentenced to death by the Bangladesh International Crimes Tribunal for "crimes against humanity" - allegedly perpetrated to quell the 'uprising' - along with Hasina in absentia.Islam said people wish to see the court orders implemented against those who are fugitives, including Hasina. "We expect India will reply and will play its role in strengthening the relations between the two countries," she said.Referring to Hasina's recent remarks that her Awami League colleagues plan to return around Dec, Islam has recently said, "If she surrenders, the existing law will be followed. She will have to go to jail."
Article Summary: Bangladesh has sent a letter to India seeking the extradition of key Sheikh Hasina aide and former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal. Kamal is said to have fled along with the former PM amid the "2024 uprising" against her govt.

Article Title: Watch: Andrew Tate appears to pass phone to team member as US Marshals arrest him over UK charges
Article Text:
Video shows Andrew Tate trying to hand mobile to his bodyguard.

Arrest linked to UK extradition request

Fresh charges filed in Britain

Romania case still ongoing

Lawyer calls arrest 'political'

A video circulating online appears to show controversial influencer Andrew Tate attempting to pass his mobile phone to a member of his entourage moments after he was arrested by US Marshals in Miami.In the footage, the 39-year-old can be seen apparently handing the device to a member of his team, who drops it before another person retrieves it. It remains unclear whether US authorities ultimately recovered the phone following the arrest.Andrew Tate and his younger brother, Tristan Tate, 38, were taken into custody in Miami on Saturday by the US Marshals Service. The arrests were made in connection with a request from British authorities, who are seeking the brothers' extradition to face criminal proceedings in the United Kingdom.The US Marshals Service confirmed the arrests but has not publicly disclosed the charges, with the arrest warrant remaining under seal.The arrests came after Britain's Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) authorised a fresh set of charges against the brothers.Andrew Tate has been charged with seven additional counts of rape, along with offences related to sex trafficking and indecent images of a child.Before the latest charges, he was already facing allegations including rape, actual bodily harm, human trafficking and controlling prostitution for gain.Tristan Tate has been charged with two additional counts of rape and three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation. He was already facing charges including rape, actual bodily harm and human trafficking.Together, the brothers now face dozens of charges linked to multiple alleged victims. They have denied all allegations against them.The Tate brothers, who have lived in Romania since 2016, are also under separate criminal investigation there over allegations including rape, human trafficking, organised crime and money laundering. They have denied wrongdoing in that case as well.Romanian authorities had previously indicated they would not extradite the brothers to the UK until domestic legal proceedings were concluded. British prosecutors subsequently moved to pursue action after learning the brothers had travelled to the United States.The brothers' attorney, Joseph D. McBride, described the arrests as politically motivated, alleging they were the result of an abuse of authority.He said the defence was confident the brothers would successfully challenge the case and argued that the United States should not carry out what he characterised as Britain's "political dirty work."British authorities are expected to submit a formal extradition request, which the Tate brothers, who hold both British and American citizenship, can challenge in US courts.
Article Summary: Video shows Andrew Tate trying to hand mobile to his bodyguard. The 39-year-old can be seen apparently handing the device to a member of his team, who drops it before another person retrieves it. Andrew Tate and his younger brother, Tristan Tate, 38, were taken into custody in Miami on Saturday by the US Marshals Service. The arrests were made in connection with a request from British authorities, who are seeking the brothers' extradition to face criminal proceedings in the UK.
