Article Title: Watch: US firefighters rescue dog that went missing after July 4th fireworks
Article Text:
Video credit: Fox news

US firefighters rescued a dog found swimming in the San Francisco Bay after it went missing on the Fourth of July. The firefighters brought it safely to the shore, according to Fox News.The Menlo Park Fire Protection District received a call on Thursday about a dog entering the water, the officials said.The first responders carried out the rescue operation using binoculars, then a drone, to locate the dog. The team reached the pup using a boat and found it paddling in the bay. The department later released footage of the dog rescue on social media.As per reports, an explosion of fireworks on the Fourth of July scared the dog off, and he ran away to escape the panic. A Facebook post by the firefighters featured several pictures of the rescue, including the black dog wrapped in a firefighter’s jacket, with a caption, “Thank you to everyone who helped reunite this furry friend with its family.”The East Palo Alto police department also released footage showing the dog being followed by seagulls in the water. According to InMenlo, the dog was rescued a half mile off the shore.Authorities later turned it over to the local Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (SPCA), which located the pup’s family and returned it.A woman claiming to be the dog’s owner thanked the fire district in a social media post. She wrote, “I want to thank the entire rescue team from the bottom of my heart. These last 2 weeks were a lot of agony not knowing about my dog.”“My heart started beating so hard when I received the call from the SPCA team. I would never be able to thank you enough for her rescue and for bringing her back to her home. Forever grateful,” she added.
Article Summary: Firefighters rescued a dog found swimming in the San Francisco Bay after it went missing on the Fourth of July. The firefighters brought it safely to the shore. An explosion of fireworks scared the dog off, and he ran away to escape the panic. The SPCA located the pup's family and returned it.

Article Title: Meet Sarah Kendzior: The bestselling author who traded her writing desk for a $17-an-hour garden centre job and found unexpected joy
Article Text:
Image: Ode

Who is Sarah Kendzior and why did she trade her desk job for a $17-an-hour garden centre job

Why did she choose to work at a garden centre

Looking back on the experience, Kendzior told CNBC, "I loved every minute."

Lessons from an unexpected career move

For many people, taking a minimum-wage or part-time job is often seen as a last resort. But for Sarah Kendzior, a 48-year-old American author and journalist, working at a local garden centre became far more than a way to supplement her income. Earning $17 (£12.50) an hour, she discovered a renewed sense of purpose, community and joy in a role that she says became one of the best jobs she has ever had. Speaking to CNBC, Kendzior reflected on how an unexpected career detour transformed her outlook on work and life.Sarah Kendzior is an American journalist, author and political commentator known for writing about authoritarianism, politics and social issues. She has written several bestselling books, including The View from Flyover Country, Hiding in Plain Sight and They Knew.Alongside her writing career, Kendzior has contributed to numerous publications and built a reputation as a respected public commentator. Despite her professional success, like many freelancers and independent writers, she has faced periods of financial uncertainty.In an interview with CNBC, she explained that taking a part-time retail job was a practical decision to help make ends meet.Rather than seeing the role as a step backwards, Kendzior embraced the opportunity to do something completely different from her usual work. She joined a local garden centre, where she spent her days helping customers, caring for plants, watering flowers and learning about gardening.The position paid $17 an hour, but she says the experience offered rewards that went well beyond the pay cheque.Working outdoors, staying physically active and interacting with customers in a friendly environment gave her a sense of satisfaction that contrasted with the solitary nature of writing.'I loved every minute,' says Sarah as she looks back at the experienceShe described the garden centre as one of the best workplaces she had experienced, praising both her colleagues and the customers she met each day. Unlike many high-pressure professional roles, the work offered immediate, tangible results, whether it was helping someone choose the right plant or watching flowers thrive under proper care. The job also encouraged a healthier routine, allowing her to spend less time behind a computer and more time outdoors.Kendzior believes her experience challenges the idea that success is defined solely by prestigious titles or high salaries. She argues that every form of honest work deserves respect and that meaningful employment can sometimes be found in the most unexpected places.Her story also reflects a wider reality in today's economy, where many professionals take on additional work to manage rising living costs or supplement freelance incomes. Rather than viewing these jobs as failures, Kendzior sees them as opportunities to learn new skills, meet different people and gain a fresh perspective on life.For her, a part-time job at a garden centre was not simply a financial necessity, it became a reminder that fulfilling work can come in many forms.
Article Summary: Sarah Kendzior, 48, is an American journalist, author and political commentator. She took a part-time job at a garden centre for $17 (£12.50) an hour. She says she found a renewed sense of purpose, community and joy in the role.

Article Title: Andrew Tate, brother Tristan Tate to fight UK extradition after appearing in US court over rape, sex trafficking charges: ‘They’ve never done nothing wrong,’ says lawyer
Article Text:
Andrew Tate, brother Tristan to fight UK extradition after appearing in US court over rape, sex trafficking charges: ‘They’ve never done nothing wrong,’ says lawyer

Brothers appear in shackles at Miami court

Next hearing scheduled for July 27

38 new charges announced in the UK

Legal troubles continue in Romania

Separate civil case in the US

Who is Andrew Tate?

Controversial influencer Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan Tate appeared in a federal courtroom in Miami on Monday as extradition proceedings to the United Kingdom formally began over a fresh set of criminal charges, including rape and sex trafficking.According to the BBC, the brothers were brought before the court after being arrested in Florida on Saturday following a request linked to new charges announced by the UK's Crown Prosecution Service (CPS).The Tate brothers, who have repeatedly denied all allegations against them, have been held in a Florida jail since their arrest.During the brief hearing, Andrew and Tristan Tate appeared wearing light brown prison uniforms. They were handcuffed and shackled at the waist and ankles.The brothers spoke only once during the proceedings, responding in unison "Yes, your honour" when the judge asked whether they understood their rights.Their attorney, Joe McBride, later told reporters that the brothers would contest the extradition request."They've never done nothing wrong. They shouldn't be extradited for crimes they didn't commit," McBride said.He went on to describe the case as "garbage" and "a stitch up job."Comparing the proceedings to the legal cases involving US President Donald Trump, McBride alleged the extradition attempt amounted to "political kidnapping" and called it a "witch hunt."According to the Associated Press, the judge scheduled the brothers' next court appearance for July 27.McBride estimated that the extradition process could take around 60 days, although any final decision on whether the brothers are sent to the UK would ultimately rest with the Trump administration.The latest case stems from 38 new criminal charges announced by the Crown Prosecution Service in England and Wales.According to CPS Special Crime Division head Malcolm McHaffie, the charges followed the receipt of additional evidence from Bedfordshire Police.The alleged offences are said to have taken place between July 2010 and August 2017 and increase the total number of alleged victims in the UK case to seven.Police said the brothers now face 59 charges in total.The UK case comes as Andrew and Tristan Tate continue to face separate criminal proceedings in Romania, where prosecutors have accused them of human trafficking, forming an organised criminal group to sexually exploit women and, in Andrew Tate's case, rape.The brothers deny all allegations.The dual British-American citizens relocated to the United States in 2025 after Romanian authorities lifted a travel ban imposed during the investigation. Despite being allowed to travel, they remain legally required to report to Romanian authorities as that case continues.In addition to the criminal investigations in the UK and Romania, the Tate brothers are also facing a civil lawsuit in the United States.A woman has alleged that the brothers coerced her into sex work before later defaming her after she cooperated with Romanian investigators.Andrew Tate rose to prominence on social media through videos showcasing luxury cars, expensive lifestyles and what he described as hyper-masculinity. The former kickboxer has repeatedly drawn criticism for controversial remarks about women and has described himself as a "misogynist."He was previously banned from several major social media platforms after making comments suggesting women should "bear responsibility" for being sexually assaulted. His accounts were later reinstated on some platforms.
Article Summary: Andrew and Tristan Tate appeared in a federal courtroom in Miami on Monday. extradition proceedings to the United Kingdom formally began over a fresh set of criminal charges, including rape and sex trafficking. The brothers were brought before the court after being arrested in Florida on Saturday following a request linked to new charges announced by the UK's Crown Prosecution Service.

Article Title: Donald Trump imposes 50% tariffs on most Canadian goods, cites trade disputes
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump announces 50% tariffs on most Canadian goods.

US President Donald Trump on Monday imposed 50% tariffs on most Canadian goods, accusing Canada of unfairly discriminating against American automobiles, alcohol and dairy products in a move that could sharply escalate trade tensions between the two countries.According to a senior administration official, the tariffs have been imposed under Section 338 of the Trade Act of 1930, after Trump signed three proclamations authorising the measures. The official said Canada was among the few countries, alongside China, that retaliated against Trump's earlier tariffs and "must be held accountable."The new tariffs exempt energy products, potash, fish and critical minerals, but apply to many goods that were previously protected under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). The trade pact, which came into force in 2020, recently expired, prompting fresh negotiations that could continue until 2036.The latest move is expected to heighten economic uncertainty, raising concerns over higher inflation and further straining ties between the United States and Canada, whose economies have long been closely integrated.The administration official, who spoke on condition of anonymity while previewing the announcement, also said Trump had directed his aides to examine the possibility of imposing additional tariffs on Canada, arguing that Canadian wildfires had worsened air quality in the United States.Last year, several Democratic lawmakers proposed repealing Section 338 of the Trade Act, arguing that the provision could be used by Trump to destabilise the US economy through unilateral tariff actions.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump imposes 50% tariffs on most Canadian goods. Trump accuses Canada of unfairly discriminating against American automobiles, alcohol and dairy products. New tariffs exempt energy products, potash, fish and critical minerals, but apply to many goods that were previously protected under the USMCA.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Usha Vance: 'There's nothing more exciting than getting to see the world through the eye of kids as they're growing up' and the joys of motherhood
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Usha Vance on motherhood.

"It’s the greatest privilege of my life. There are so many exciting things that happen in life, but there is nothing more exciting than getting to see the world through the eyes of kids as they’re growing up. Everything is just more exciting with my children around, and everything is more meaningful.

There’s virtually nothing that I do in a given day that means as much as seeing them learn something new, seeing them grow into being a better person, helping shape a future where they will be able to do the same things that I’m doing today," Usha Vance said.

Ewan, Vivek, Mirabel and Alec

On having a fourth child

Second Lady Usha Vance has recently welcomed her fourth child, Alec Neel Vance, with Vice President JD Vance. But Usha Vance spoke about the joys of motherhood on several occasions. In her Mother's Day message this year, as she was expecting Alec, she issued a profound yet simple statement that summarized what becoming a mother meant to Vance.The Vances are now parents to four children:Usha Vance has spoken extensively about motherhood, about embracing it for the 4th time after the Vances announced the pregnancy.“People have asked me if we’re going to have a fourth baby, and I’ve never closed the door on that. I grew up in a family of two, and I thought that was a great number. And then I had two kids, and I thought — I didn’t feel quite done, right? So I really wanted to have a third child," Usha Vance said in an NBC interview.“We have our daughter, who’s amazing, and it was great. And so I just wasn’t sure. But as time passed, I realized that I was feeling more and more, kind of, excited about that possibility. And so if there was a chance, I should take it. I knew that I’d be happy if we only had three kids, and I knew that I’d be happy if we had four. And so here we are.”On another occasion, Usha Vance spoke about being a working mom earlier and now being the Second Lady and said: “The balancing act today is sometimes easier than it was when I was working full-time in the private sector because I have more control over my schedule and do not feel pulled in as many directions. That said, raising children in the public eye poses new challenges. While I certainly miss working, I am grateful that I have the time to ensure that our home life is as normal and stable as possible.First-generation American Usha Vance was born to immigrant parents in San Diego, California. Her father is a retired mechanical engineer who went on to become a lecturer at San Diego State University, while her mother is the provost of the University of California San Diego's Sixth College and has a background in marine molecular biology. Usha has a younger sister, Shreya Chilukuri.
Article Summary: Usha Vance has recently welcomed her fourth child, Alec Neel Vance, with Vice President JD Vance. Vance has spoken extensively about motherhood, about embracing it for the 4th time after the Vances announced the pregnancy. In her Mother's Day message this year, as she was expecting Alec, she issued a profound yet simple statement that summarized what becoming a mother meant to Vance.

Article Title: US judge halts Paramount-Warner Bros merger for 14 days amid antitrust challenge by 12 states
Article Text: A federal judge in California on Monday temporarily blocked Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery from completing their proposed $110 billion merger, granting a 14-day restraining order as a multistate antitrust lawsuit challenging the deal moves forward.The order prevents the companies from closing the transaction until at least August 3, when the court will hear arguments on a preliminary injunction that could bar the merger from being completed until a final ruling is issued.In her ruling, the judge said the states had raised "serious questions" about whether the merger could reduce competition, adding that "the balance of equities and public interest tip sharply in favor of the Plaintiff States."The legal challenge was filed last week by 12 Democratic-led states, headed by California, in a direct challenge to the Trump administration's Justice Department, which approved the merger in June.California Attorney General Rob Bonta welcomed the court's decision, calling the temporary restraining order "a critical first win in our case to ensure this megamerger never sees the light of day."According to the lawsuit, the combined company would control about 27% of wide-release theatrical film distribution in the United States and a similar share of the basic cable channel licensing market.The states argue that combining two of Hollywood's five major film distributors would reduce competition, resulting in higher prices, lower quality, and less content for consumers."California and our sister states are fighting for free and fair markets, not rigged markets. America has no kings in government or our economy," Bonta said.Paramount rejected the allegations, maintaining that the transaction would strengthen competition in the media industry.A Paramount spokesperson told Variety that the company is "grateful for the Court’s swift order" and said it "preserves the status quo while the Court considers the antitrust issues presented."The spokesperson added: "This merger is lawful, pro-competitive, and will benefit consumers, creators, workers, and the entertainment industry.""We will continue to vigorously defend the transaction and will look forward to the hearings on the substance of the State AGs’ action."The proposed merger, approved by the Trump administration on June 12 without requiring any changes, would create one of the world's largest entertainment companies. The combined group would include assets such as CNN, Warner Bros. Pictures, and the HBO Max streaming service.The deal also carries political implications, with President Donald Trump saying he would weigh in on the merger as the future of CNN, a frequent target of his criticism, remains uncertain.The acquisition represents a major victory for media executive David Ellison, whose takeover bid was largely financed by his father, Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, a Trump ally.The bidding war for Warner Bros. began last year when Netflix and Paramount competed to acquire the studio. Netflix eventually withdrew its offer in February after Paramount continued to raise its bid, paving the way for the proposed merger.
Article Summary: A federal judge in California temporarily blocks Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery from completing their proposed $110 billion merger. The order prevents the companies from closing the transaction until at least August 3, when the court will hear arguments on a preliminary injunction. The legal challenge was filed last week by 12 Democratic-led states, headed by California.

Article Title: Tina Sodhi paid $2,000 for wellness treatment in Florida, she never made it home; doctor charged with manslaughter a year later
Article Text:
A year after Tina Sodhi's death, a doctor at a Miami health center has been charged with manslaughter.

Heart Protocol Ceremony

51-year-old Tina Sodhi was found unresponsive on February 10, 2025, at a wellness home where she took part in a three-day wellness retreat for which she paid $2,000. After over a year, Dr Samul Lee has now been arrested on a second-degree felony manslaughter as medical examiners found that Sodhi was administered drugs like MDMA, ketamine which contributed to the dehydration also caused by prolonged heat exposure inside the sauna. Dehydration was revealed to be the cause of the death.The wellness program that Sodhi took at Sabia Wellness was called Heart Protocol Ceremony, described as a treatment to help participants connect with their higher selves. Sodhi was also made to sign a waiver acknowledging that her participation was voluntary and that she understood the potential risks and side effects of the substances used.During the investigation, Miami Beach police consulted an independent physician, who concluded that Lee's conduct "reflects an extreme and unjustifiable deviation from accepted safety and clinical practices," court documents state.Lee's attorney last week entered a plea of not guilty and requested a jury trial. His medical license in Texas has been temporarily suspended, with a board calling his “practice of medicine a threat to public welfare.”Attorney Richard Cooper representing the owner of Sabia Wellness House said: “We are grateful that the police and the state attorneys office saw this case for what it is and what it is not and that my client was not liable in any way for this tragedy.There are some great effective alternatives to western medicine but tragedy unfolds when not performed to the utmost standards.”CBS News Miami reported that they visited the property where the ceremony was held but the owner was not present. The father of the owner said his daughter was out of the country. Court documents indicated that the owner also participated in the Heart Protocol ceremony.
Article Summary: 51-year-old Tina Sodhi was found unresponsive on February 10, 2025, at a wellness home where she took part in a three-day wellness retreat for which she paid $2,000. Dr Samul Lee has now been arrested on a second-degree felony manslaughter as medical examiners found that SodHI was administered drugs like MDMA, ketamine which contributed to the dehydration also caused by prolonged heat exposure.

Article Title: Unlicensed doctor arrested in New York after woman dies from anti-ageing injection
Article Text:
Luis Rojas Cabrera

An unlicensed doctor has been arrested in New York after a 27-year-old woman died after receiving an anti-ageing serum injection at a holistic wellness centre in the Bronx.Elizabeth Baron lost consciousness shortly after undergoing the procedure at the Bereshit Lifestyle Centre on Riverdale Avenue near West 232nd Street at around noon on Sunday, the New York Post reported, citing police and sources.She was taken to NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital, where she was pronounced dead at about 1.10pm.Police arrested 55-year-old Luis Rojas Cabrera later that day and charged him with reckless endangerment and the unauthorised practice of a profession.Sources told the NYP that Cabrera is licensed to practise medicine in the Dominican Republic but does not hold a medical licence in the United States.On the wellness centre's website, Rojas describes himself as an "M.D., Surgeon, Naturopath" and claims to be U.S. board certified in holistic health and alternative medicine. He also says he is a full member of several medical organisations in the Dominican Republic and the Hispanic Health Professionals Association of New York. The website states that he comes from a family of medical professionals in the Dominican Republic and began assisting his mother with nursing and medical procedures at the age of 11, an experience he says inspired him to pursue a career in medicine.The city's Office of Chief Medical Examiner is conducting a toxicology report to determine the cause of Baron's death.
Article Summary: Elizabeth Baron lost consciousness shortly after undergoing the procedure at the Bereshit Lifestyle Centre in the Bronx. She was taken to NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital, where she was pronounced dead at about 1.10pm. Luis Rojas Cabrera, 55, has been charged with reckless endangerment and the unauthorised practice of a profession.

Article Title: 'Will not be arrested in US': Trump responds to Mamdani's Netanyahu remarks
Article Text:
Benjamin Netanyahu and Donald Trump

US President Donald Trump on Monday said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu would not face arrest in the United States, responding to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's remarks that the Israeli leader could be detained during his visit for the United Nations General Assembly in September.This is not the first time Mamdani, a vocal critic of Netanyahu over Israel's war in Gaza, has spoken about "arresting" him in New York City."Benjamin Netanyahu will not be arrested, in any way, shape, or form, while in the United States of America. He is fighting against the Islamic Republic of Iran, which recently killed 52,000 innocent protestors, and has spent the last 47 years killing American soldiers, and others," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform."The only ones that should be arrested are the people that led Iran into this unprecedented SPIRAL OF DEATH AND DESTRUCTION, something that should have been dealt with years ago, by previous Presidents!" he added.Trump's remarks came after Mamdani said his administration was examining whether it had any legal authority to act against Netanyahu when the Israeli prime minister visits New York City. However, the mayor clarified that any potential arrest would only be carried out under an existing law.Netanyahu faces an International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrant over alleged "crimes against humanity" in Gaza. The warrant means he could be arrested if he enters the territory of a country that is party to the ICC."Whatever the law allows me to do in New York City, that's what we will do, but we won't be writing our own laws to that end. I believe Prime Minister Netanyahu belongs in The Hague. He's a war criminal who has been charged by the International Criminal Court," Mamdani told The New York Times in an interview.The ICC is based in The Hague, Netherlands.
Article Summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has spoken about "arresting" Benjamin Netanyahu during his visit to the United Nations in September. President Donald Trump said Netanyahu would not face arrest in the United States. Netanyahu faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over alleged "crimes against humanity" in Gaza.

Article Title: 'Will pay many times over': Trump warns Iran after US troop deaths in Jordan
Article Text: US President Donald Trump on Monday warned that Iran would face a heavy response for every American soldier killed, following the deaths of two US service members in an Iranian missile and drone attack in Jordan.In a post on Truth Social, Trump said he had directed secretary of defense Pete Hegseth, chairman of the joint chiefs of staff gen. Daniel Caine and other military leaders to ensure a harsher response."Every time Iran kills an American Soldier they will pay for that killing many times over! This directive has been passed on to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Daniel Caine, and every Leader in the Military," Trump said.The remarks came after two US service members were killed and another remained missing following an Iranian ballistic missile and drone attack on a military base in Jordan, marking the first American troop deaths from direct Iranian fire since the opening days of the war.The US military said the troops were killed on Friday while US and partner forces were defending the base against the Iranian attack. Four other service members who were medically evacuated to hospitals in Jordan have since been discharged.The Pentagon identified the two personnel killed as 1st Lt. Tyler James Feehan, 25, of Ewa Beach, Hawaii, and Pvt. Isabella Gonzales, 19, of Carrollton, Texas. They had been deployed in support of the US mission against the Islamic State group.According to the US military, 17 American service members have been killed since the war with Iran began.Meanwhile, the US military’s Central Command on Monday said its ninth straight night of airstrikes targeted “Iranian military command centers, air defense and coastal surveillance sites, maritime capabilities, missile and drone launch sites and communications networks.”Iran's state-run IRNA news agency reported that the American strikes killed at least one person around Tabriz, a northwestern city about 520 kilometers (325 miles) from the capital, Tehran. Tabriz is believed to host underground missile bases run by Iran's paramilitary Revolutionary Guard.US strikes likely also hit Bandar Imam Khomeini in Khuzestan province, Sirik and Jask in Hormozgan province and Konarak and Chahbahar in Sistan and Baluchistan province, IRNA reported.The British military's United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations center said Monday evening that a second ship had been attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, this one off the coast of the United Arab Emirates.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump warned that Iran would face a heavy response for every American soldier killed. Trump said he had directed secretary of defense Pete Hegseth, chairman of the joint chiefs of staff gen. Daniel Caine and other military leaders to ensure a harsher response. Two US service members were killed and another remained missing following an Iranian ballistic missile and drone attack on a military base in Jordan.

Article Title: 16 days after Nolan Wells' death, no one knows what exactly happened to the Mississippi footballer who went to Horn Island with friends
Article Text:
Mississippi footballer Nolan Wells' memorial service was held on Monday.

Drowning not ruled out but family hires attorney for separate investigation

The memorial service of Nolan Wells, the Mississippi teen who died during a Fourth of July outing to Horn Island, is to be livestreamed today as the mysterious case grabbed nationwide attention because of the race of Wells. Wells was the only Black among the friend group and the rest of them made it back home. Wells' body was found on July 6, face down in the water.Wells was a 2025 graduate and multi-sport athlete at Ocean Springs High School and later played football at Southwest Mississippi Community College.Actor and media mogul Tyler Perry is paying for the services, according to CBS News.While investigators have said drowning is suspected, they haven't released an official cause of death, and the case remains under investigation.There was no sign of trauma or foul play on Well's body but the autopsy result has not been revealed as the experts are now waiting for toxicology test. Wells’ parents sent their son’s body out of state for an independent autopsy, family attorney Ben Crump said.“We had his body flown from Mississippi to Washington, DC, because his family wanted to make sure that they had a doctor who had no ties to Mississippi law enforcement to do an independent examination of their son’s body,” Crump said.This autopsy result is also awaited.The other three friends have retained attorneys. One of the friends said Well stayed back with a girl he met. “They met that day, and it was kind of – it’s kind of one of those things. … he really did like her, but that was the only time they ever hung out was at Horn Island on July 4,” Tracestin Shepherd said. But another friend who also saw Wells on July 4 said it was not like Wells to separate from the group he came with.Wells’ mother, Christine Wells-Wonsley, said the family compared the location history between the Snapchat and Life360 apps tracking her son’s phone – but the data didn’t match.Shepherd said the friends are now receiving death threats. “We did no wrong here, and we don’t understand how we’re getting so much hate behind us,” he said. “We all cared (for) and loved Nolan, and nobody wanted to see Nolan die. Nobody wanted to see his life be taken so short.”
Article Summary: Drowning not ruled out but family hires attorney for separate investigation. Wells was a 2025 graduate and multi-sport athlete at Ocean Springs High School and later played football at Southwest Mississippi Community College. Actor and media mogul Tyler Perry is paying for the services.

Article Title: Race back to US: September 15 cutoff for F-1 students seeking ‘duration of status’ protection
Article Text:
September 15 cutoff for F-1 students seeking ‘duration of status’ protection

The final rule issued recently by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has replaced the long-standing ‘duration of status’ (D/S) regime (whereby students could stay in the US as long as they were studying) with fixed periods of admission of a maximum of four years. Post the expiry of this fixed period, visa extensions need to be sought. The final rule will come into effect from Sept 15.Currently international students, studying in the US are covered by the D/S regime. Immigration attorneys state that such students who are visiting India or are holiday in another country must return to the US before Sept 15, if they want to benefit from the transition provisions.Following publication of the final rules, DHS has issued a fact sheet and FAQs. The agency has clarified that students already in the US under D/S on the rule's effective date can continue to remain until their programme end date on their Form I-20 or the end of approved OPT/STEM OPT. However, this is subject to an overall cap of four years from the effective date – (it cannot exceed Nov 14, 2030, which is four years plus a 60-day departure period). Immigration attorneys caution that this protection is available only to students who are physically present in the US on Sept 15.New York-based immigration attorney Karin Wolman said, “An F-1 visa holder who is currently outside the US must return by Sept 15 (preferably arrive on Sept 14 to accommodate flight delays) in order to be covered by the transition rules and be readmitted with a duration of status on their I-94 (which is the arrival and departure record).”Rajiv S. Khanna, managing attorney at Immigration.com, echoed the advice. "A student admitted to the US on or before Sept 14 falls under the old duration-of-status framework. If that same student is physically present in the US and maintaining status on Sept 15, the transition provision lets them remain based on the programme end date on the Form I-20, subject to the four-year cap," he said, adding that students entering on or after Sept 15 will instead receive a fixed ‘admit-until’ date on their I-94.“Be mindful that entering early secures this D/S position only until the first trip abroad after the effective date. The advantage is real, but it is fragile,”’ added Khanna."The four-year transition period does not automatically give students four extra years in the US. It simply allows D/S to continue for up to four years, provided the student continues to maintain valid F-1 status. If the academic programme ends and the applicable grace period expires, the student falls out of status and begins accruing unlawful presence. In short, four years is a cap on D/S, not a guarantee of four years of authorized stay," pointed out Cyrus D. Mehta, a New York based immigration attorney.The rule also has important implications for students already in the US who later travel outside the US. In this regard, DHS has stated that students who leave the US after the rule takes effect and subsequently return "may be admitted with a new fixed period of admission", based on the programme end date on the Form I-20, capped at four years, along with a 30-day departure period.Form I-20 is the official document issued by a US educational institute that certifies a student has been admitted to a full-time academic programme and is eligible for an F-1 student visa. Under the new rule, the programme end date on the Form I-20 becomes even more significant because DHS says students admitted after Sept 15, will generally receive an I-94 authorizing them to remain until the programme end date shown on the I-20 (subject to a maximum of four years)."A student presently in the US and covered by the transition rules loses D/S and the 60-day grace period if they travel abroad any time after Sept 15. A student returning after the Christmas holidays, for instance, will receive a date-certain I-94 and only a 30-day grace period," explained Wolman.Khanna described this as "a problem area for the unwary". He said any student who departs and re-enters after the rule takes effect will be inspected under the new system, irrespective of the earlier D/S admission. " The student does not lose F-1 status, but the open-ended D/S admission is replaced by a fixed date on the I-94," he said.Mehta added that re-entry after Sept 15 could also reduce the post-study grace period from 60 days to 30 days. “If the student stays beyond the fixed admission period plus the 30 days, they would start accruing unlawful presence and could potentially trigger the 3- and 10-year re-entry bars,” he cautioned
Article Summary: The final rule will come into effect from Sept 15. Currently international students, studying in the US are covered by the D/S regime. Immigration attorneys state that students who are visiting India or are holiday in another country must return to the US before Sept 15, if they want to benefit from the transition provisions.

Article Title: 'Cherry-picking numbers': Trump admin slams report claiming Pentagon withheld data on troop injuries in Iran war
Article Text:
NYT report says injuries under reported in US-Iran War, Pentagon denies allegation

More than 400 US troops injured since war began

Pentagon denies withholding information

Pentagon protocols and presidential response

The Pentagon has allegedly withheld information about dozens of American service members injured in Iranian strikes on US bases in Jordan, The New York Times reported.In the week before Friday's attack that killed two US soldiers and left another missing, Iran carried out three other strikes against US forces in Jordan, according to several US officials. Those strikes wounded dozens of troops and damaged several helicopters, the officials said.These injuries were never disclosed by the Pentagon.A US military official told the NYT that Central Command is not obligated to release information about injured service members, particularly when they return to duty quickly. Another official said the Pentagon would not share information that could help Iran fine-tune its attacks on bases housing thousands of American troops.More than 400 US service members have been wounded in the Iran conflict, according to Central Command. The Pentagon had previously reported the total number of troops injured and returned to duty, but has stopped updating that figure in recent weeks.In a Saturday statement, Central Command said four American troops wounded in Friday's attack were taken to Jordanian hospitals and had been discharged. It said more troops received minor injuries and returned to duty, but did not specify how many.The statement did not mention troops injured in the three earlier strikes in Jordan last week.Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell rejected the NYT report, calling it "baseless and malicious accusations" and "outright lies from partisan hacks at the New York Times.""The Department of War rejects these baseless and malicious accusations of hiding injury numbers as outright lies from partisan hacks at the New York Times who are desperate to smear America's military and its leadership," Parnell said.He added: "Claims of concealment are fabrications meant to further distress the American people in the wake of three service members killed in action. Disgusting behavior, even for the New York Times."Parnell said US military casualty information is publicly available and regularly updated online on the Defense Casualty Analysis System for everyone, including the media, to review. He also argued that "injuries in the military encompass everything from minor sprained ankles during routine training to incidents entirely unrelated to combat operations. Cherry-picking raw numbers without context paints a deliberately misleading and incomplete picture. "He said the military was "the most transparent Department of War in history" and challenged the "so-called journalists who wrote these lies" to "stop the smears against the finest warfighting force on Earth."The Pentagon's casualty reporting protocols require publicly identifying deceased service members only after 24 hours have passed since next of kin were notified. The names of troops wounded in action are not typically released.In a brief phone call with NewsNation, President Trump said the troops died "in service of our country" and reiterated the war's primary goal of "never allowing Iran to have a nuclear weapon."The deaths of two Army soldiers in Jordan on Friday and another in northern Iraq bring to 17 the total number of US military personnel killed since the US and Israel launched attacks on Iran on February 28.
Article Summary: Pentagon denies allegations that it withheld information about injuries in Iran war. Official: Pentagon would not share information that could help Iran fine- tune its attacks on bases. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell calls the allegations "baseless and malicious accusations"

Article Title: Father saved for years so that I could study in America but...: Woman's 'American Dream' turns into 'Make in India'
Article Text:
Indian woman who moved to Germany after losing visa status in the US says she's considering a future in India.

From American Dream to Make in India

Ananya Joshi went to the US in 2022 to pursue her master's. She got a job but her employer could not sponsor her H-1B visa and eventually, she had to leave the US. But now after working in Germany, Joshi is in two minds about returning to the US because the uncertainty is still there. Instead, she wants to go back to India and start something of her own. In an interview with Business Insider, Joshi explained how dear the American Dream was to her. She grew up seeing a little Statue of Liberty souvenir. Her father saved for years to finance her American degree, as it was initially his dream that he could not fulfil.In 2022, Ananya moved to Illinois for her master's in biotechnology at Northwestern University; she graduated in 2024, worked for some time on F1 OPT and then had to leave her $ 75,000-a-year job."My company, which had initially promised to help me apply for an H-1B visa, realized it couldn't keep the promise. The company said it couldn't complete E-Verify, the federal employment verification system. My OPT was about to expire in July 2025, and I wasn't able to devote time to job hunting because of my heavy workload. In May 2025, I told the company I would like to resign or work part-time because I need those last two months to figure things out.I got let go the next day," Joshi said."I started applying for jobs in cities around the world, focusing mostly on the US but also in Europe, Canada, and Australia. Even after getting about 20 interviews and making it to the fourth round multiple times, I was still not getting a job. This took place between May and July 2025, when immigration turbulence was starting to rise in the US.""I got two job offers, one from a company in Germany and the other from Canada. People around me spoke highly about the stability of Germany and all its labor laws, and having gone through so much, I realized I needed that stability. So, in January this year, I moved to Rostock, a small city about three hours north of Berlin, to work at another lab-grown meat startup," Joshi said.Life in a small city in Germany, compared to New Delhi and ChicagoJoshi said life never seemed slow in New Delhi and Chicago and so adjusting to a small city in Germany has been difficult. But Rostock is cleaner, safer with walkable streets, a beautiful beach and a jungle train. "But it's a small place, and there's not that much to do. The language barrier is a problem too; English is spoken at work, but it's all in German outside. I've started taking German classes," she said."It's also not the best place for connectivity. The nearest airports are Hamburg and Berlin, both more than three hours away. As an immigrant, being able to travel easily matters a lot to me, especially if I need to fly out quickly."Joshi's boyfriend is in the US and she said she's super confused about what the future holds. One part of her wants to go back to the US but "I can't forget what I went through. It doesn't feel smart to move back until things look more promising", she said. So instead of the set path of H-1B to Green Card, she is now considering a future in India -- in Mumbai or Bangalore. "India is close to the US in terms of opportunities, and there is so much potential to continue growing my career there," she said.
Article Summary: Ananya Joshi went to the US in 2022 to pursue her master's. She got a job but her employer could not sponsor her H-1B visa and eventually, she had to leave the US. Now after working in Germany, Joshi is in two minds about returning to US because the uncertainty is still there. She wants to go back to India and start something of her own.

Article Title: Trump scores own-goal as World Cup overflows with politics
Article Text:
Trump at FIFA World Cup

TOI correspondent from Washington:

Spain won the World Cup but Donald Trump nearly stole the moment of glory.For a few awkward seconds after Spain defeated Argentina to capture football's biggest prize, the victorious Spaniards found themselves sharing the podium with an American president who remained planted centre stage like an enthusiastic wedding guest who has wandered into the family photograph and refuses to take the hint.The cue to leave eventually came from FIFA president Gianni Infantino, who, with the delicate touch of a maître d' telling a late diner it’s closing time, gently shepherded Trump away from the celebrating players.Trump's exit, as natural for him as conceding an election, was an appropriately surreal finale to a tournament over which the US President hovered like an VAR review. Earlier, as he strode onto the field for the trophy presentation, many of the 80,000-plus spectators greeted him with lusty boos, though supporters generated enough cheers to produce something closer to surround sound than consensus.There was delicious irony in the final result too. The man who has spent weeks describing Spain as "hopeless" suddenly found himself handing the World Cup to... Spain. Only days after verbally slide-tackling Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez over Nato spending, Trump had to congratulate the Spanish leader after La Roja's triumph, perhaps the fastest recorded transition from geopolitical sniping to sportsmanship since Henry Kissinger discovered table tennis ahead of a China outreach.Of course, had Argentina won, the political script would have read differently. Argentine President Javier Milei, Trump's ideological soulmate and favourite chainsaw-wielding libertarian, skipped the final because of a superstition that watching from anywhere other than home would jinx the Albiceleste.Even Lionel Messi couldn't dribble past that curse. Instead, socialist Spain prevailed over libertarian Argentina, giving the global left bragging rights in football after the global right enjoyed the spectacle of a Trump-hosted cage fight that passes off as sport.The VIP suite itself resembled a G-7 summit with better snacks. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum sat alongside Trump despite relations remaining frosty after months of tariff threats and border disputes. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney was there too, though Trump reportedly found time between crosses and corners to suggest Canada might compensate America for wildfire smoke -- or perhaps pay in tariffs.Because nothing says "the beautiful game" quite like discussing ugly trade disputes during injury time. Also in attendance was NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani -- probably relishing Socialist Spain’s victory. It was the second Trump-Mamdani cameo in a sporting arena sans meeting after Game 3 of the NBA finals.Throughout the tournament Trump's administration was as omnipresent as stadium hot dogs. Cabinet secretaries seemed to rotate through matches with the frequency of midfield substitutions, while Trump's personal appeal to Infantino after US striker Folarin Balogun's red card led FIFA to review – and ultimately soften – the suspension. Trump insisted he merely requested another look; critics saw a presidential phone-a-friend.The tournament itself occasionally resembled a dress rehearsal for the Olympics directed by three different producers. There were transportation hiccups, security bottlenecks, high ticket prices, and persistent complaints from Iran over visa problems and what it viewed as distinctly unfriendly treatment. The World Cup may have promised open play, but for some visitors America's immigration system preferred a defensive wall.Yet the apocalyptic forecast by pessimists never arrived. Instead, Boston ran out of beers after the Scots tanked up with the desperation of vehicle owners anticipating a hike in petrol prices, Kansas City's hotels became temporary Dutch colonies, and Germans chowed down the last Philly cheese steaks. Restaurant owners, hoteliers and shopkeepers discovered that football fans spend money with almost as much enthusiasm as they spend ninety minutes explaining the offside rule. For once, economists admited that the ball really did bounce in everyone's favour despite the Trump threat to bounce out dodgy visitors.The US President now says he wants the World Cup to return to the United States immediately -- and ideally remain there forever. "You hear that, Gianni?" he joked. It's an appealing fantasy, though about as likely as New Jersey hosting Oscars. The World Cup rotates continents precisely because the rest of the planet also likes throwing enormous parties every four years. See y'all in Spain, Portugal, and Morocco in 2030!
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump attended the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina. He sat alongside Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Trump reportedly found time between crosses and corners to suggest Canada might compensate America for wildfire smoke -- or perhaps pay in tariffs.

Article Title: California can store 1,000 years of carbon underground to fight climate change, but 8,000 abandoned oil wells could change everything
Article Text:
Image Credit: By PutTheKettleOn - Own work, CC BY 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=158089453

Does California have enough underground space for its CO2 emissions



Image Credit: By Jennifer Woodard Maderazo from Barcelona, Spain - Effects of coal mining, CC BY 2.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=4136744

What happens when carbon meets California’s 8,000 old wells



What rules are in place to keep the local community safe from CO2 leakage



Can this carbon storage technology help the local economy of California



Image Credit: By Implicit Matrix - Own work, CC BY 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=181084555

Is carbon capture a ‘false solution’



So, will it work



California’s fight against climate change is now being confronted by a complex challenge. As the state targets carbon neutrality by 2045, scientists suggest that capturing carbon dioxide and burying it deep underground is essential. Norway has successfully adapted this technology beneath the North Sea, but towns in California like those in Kern County present a challenge of a ‘landscape filled with over 8,000 abandoned oil wells.’ These wells act like straws poked into the Earth, potentially offering escape routes for stored gases.Can a modern carbon capture plant truly function in such a porous environment? Using insights from Stanford University and California state experts, we explore whether California can turn its oil fields into high-tech carbon storage units, or if these historic wells will lead to dangerous gas leaks.According to a joint study by Stanford University and the Energy Futures Initiative , California possesses one of the largest underground storage potentials in the United States. The state’s unique geology, particularly in the Central Valley, features thick layers of sands and shales that are perfect for trapping gases. Experts estimate that California has enough underground capacity to store its current annual emissions for over 1,000 years.To reach the goal of carbon neutrality, the Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) suggests the state must remove and store roughly 125 million metric tons of carbon dioxide every year.While this sounds like a massive undertaking, the technology is already mature and being deployed in other parts of the world. However, the success of these projects depends on whether the carbon stays where we put it.The biggest worry for residents in towns like Bakersfield is the large number of old oil and gas wells. These wells were often drilled decades ago with different levels of quality control. A study provided by the U.S. Department of Energy (OSTI) warns that every well is a potential leak path for the protective rock layer of a storage site.However, modern computer modelling provides a solution. When researchers carried out a mock experiment in the San Joaquin Valley with 1,000 legacy wells, they found that even if no repairs were made, the amount of carbon that might leak back out was less than 0.00004% of the total gas injected over 100 years. The study suggests that the most effective way to manage this risk is not just to fix every well, but to identify and seal the shakiest wells first. This would involve using historical records and modern sensors to find the wells most likely to fail.California has developed some of the strictest rules in the world to oversee these projects. The California Air Resources Board (CARB) and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) requires developers to follow a rigorous ‘CCS Protocol.’ This includes a mandatory 50-year monitoring period after the project stops injecting gas to ensure the site remains stable.Before a company like California Resources Corporation (CRC) can start their ‘ Carbon TerraVault’ project, they must prove they have the exclusive right to use the underground space and that they have studied the rock layers extensively to prevent leaks.The Stanford and EFI study points out that the industrial sector in California supports over 1.3 million jobs. Many of these workers have skills from the oil and gas industry that are directly transferable to carbon capture.By re-fitting existing power plants and factories with carbon capture equipment, the state can keep these facilities running while drastically reducing their pollution. Furthermore, building the necessary pipelines and storage hubs could create a whole new ‘clean industry’ sector. For towns with high unemployment and a history of energy production, this transition could offer a way to maintain their economic base while moving away from traditional oil drilling.There is a disagreement between scientists and community advocates. While the Stanford study and LLNL view carbon capture as a critical tool to fight global warming, some community groups are concerned that carbon capture might allow oil companies to keep extracting fossil fuels for longer than they should.The lawsuit filed in Kern County highlights that many people in ‘frontline communities’ like low-income residents who already live with high pollution, feel like they are being asked to take on the risks of a new technology while the benefits go to big corporations. This conflict shows that technology alone isn't enough; the state must also build trust and ensure that these projects provide real health and economic benefits to the people living right above the storage sites.The evidence from government and academic sources suggests that carbon capture in a town with thousands of abandoned wells is technically possible, provided that the right management strategies are used. While the risk of leaks can never be zero, modelling shows it can be minimised to a far safer level. However, the real test won't just be in the rock layers, but in the courtrooms of California. As the state moves forward with its first projects, the world will be watching to see if it can successfully bury the carbon to protect its future.
Article Summary: California has one of the largest underground storage potentials in the United States. The state’s unique geology, particularly in the Central Valley, features thick layers of sands and shales that are perfect for trapping gases. Experts estimate that California has enough underground capacity to store its current annual emissions for over 1,000 years.

Article Title: 'Failed, inhumane policy': Baloch activist raises alarm over spike in student disappearances in region

A recent surge in the alleged enforced disappearances of students and young people in Pakistan's Balochistan province has raised fresh concerns over the treatment of those linked to peaceful political organisations. Human rights activist Sammi Deen Baloch expressed her condemnation of the events and alleged that individuals are being taken from their homes, hostels and educational institutions.In a statement posted on X, Baloch described the development as alarming and a part of a broader pattern of enforced disappearances that has persisted in the restive province."The cycle of enforced disappearances in Balochistan has never truly stopped, but over the past few days in particular, there has been an alarmingly dangerous surge in the enforced disappearances of students," she said in a statement posted on X.The activist alleged that the disappearances were being justified as part of counter-insurgency operations, but argued that the approach had failed to bring peace to the restive province. Instead, she said, decades of such policies had deepened resentment and contributed to a cycle of unrest and violence."Abducting unarmed and innocent students, as well as young people affiliated with peaceful political organizations, from their homes, hostels, and educational institutions and forcibly making them disappear, and then justifying this oppression in the name of counter-insurgency, is a failed and inhumane state policy that has been imposed on Balochistan for decades," Baloch said, "If this approach were truly a means to bring peace, Balochistan would not be drowning today in this quagmire of blood, unrest, and hatred; rather, the reality is that this policy is not fostering peace but giving birth to even more hatred and violence.Baloch further alleged that young people were being held for years without being charged or brought before a court, and subjected to torture, humiliation and other forms of mistreatment. She argued that such treatment could itself fuel anger and a desire for revenge among those affected."When young people are held for years in state torture chambers without any crime or judicial process, subjected to inhuman violence, humiliation, and torment, it is the state itself that nurtures feelings of revenge and hatred against it through its own policies," she said.According to Baloch, when some of those who later reappear eventually turn to armed violence, state propaganda campaigns focus on those who speak out against enforced disappearances rather than examining the circumstances that may have contributed to the radicalisation of young people.She accused authorities of attempting to make the issue of enforced disappearances controversial by blaming peaceful political activists and human rights defenders for allegedly inciting people or recruiting them for armed groups.Baloch argued that the underlying causes of the continuing conflict were instead "illegal actions, state repression, and tyrannical policies", which she said continued to fuel hostility towards the state.She urged the authorities to review what she described as failed, unconstitutional and oppressive policies, and questioned why decades of alleged repression, enforced disappearances, extrajudicial killings and collective punishment had failed to establish lasting peace in Balochistan."Instead of offloading the burden of its failed, unconstitutional, and oppressive policies onto the shoulders of the oppressed people and political and human rights activists, the state should ask itself why, despite decades of repression, enforced disappearances, extrajudicial killings, and collective punishments, peace could not be established in Balochistan."The Pakistani government has previously rejected allegations of systematic enforced disappearances, maintaining that its security operations are conducted in accordance with the law and are aimed at combating militancy and maintaining public order.

Article Title: HIV outbreak in Pakistan: How deadly safety lapses at Sindh hospital put children at risk
Article Text:
The SHCC's regulatory inspection found that used needles were not being disposed of in sharps bins, hospital staff could not explain disposal of needles (Photo credit: ANI)

At least 78 children have contracted HIV in an outbreak in Pakistan's Karachi linked to serious infection-control and medical waste management failures at a state-run hospital.Findings at the Sindh Employees Social Security Institution (SESSI)-run Valika Hospital in Karachi's SITE area revealed needles manually removed from syringes, inadequate sterilisation safeguards and untrained staff handling contaminated waste.The Sindh Healthcare Commission (SHCC), which conducted a regulatory inspection of the state-run hospital, found that used needles were not being disposed of in sharps bins. That hospital staff could not explain where the removed needles had gone or how they had been disposed of."This raised serious concerns about the hospital's medical waste management practices, as it was unclear where the removed needles had gone or how they had been disposed of," the healthcare commission said.The findings came after a major HIV outbreak at the hospital infected 78 children and led to the screening of more than 10,500 people living in the surrounding area.A further 120 people tested positive for HIV, while six deaths have been reported, according to Dawn.Independent inquiries into the outbreak found widespread failures in infection-prevention practices, including the dangerous reuse of single-use syringes. The findings have raised fresh questions over the safety of medical procedures and the handling of infectious waste at one of Sindh's state-run hospitals.During its inspection, the SHCC found that technical personnel were unable to tell inspectors how contaminated medical waste was being disposed of. The hospital had also failed to provide formal safety training to staff or produce written guidelines for handling medical waste and following infection-control procedures.The condition of the hospital's autoclave, a machine used to sterilise medical equipment, could not be verified. Nursing staff and operation theatre personnel were also absent from their posts during duty hours, making it difficult for inspectors to assess routine infection-control practices."The working condition of the autoclave could not be verified during the visit. Nursing and operation theatre (OT) staffs were also not available during duty time, which was making it difficult to assess routine infection control practices of their duty places," the regulatory body added.The SHCC also found that medical waste was not being segregated and disposed of according to infection prevention and control guidelines. Hospital staff had poor knowledge of safe medical waste handling, while the private contractor responsible for collecting and disposing of the waste had not received proper training."The team found that medical waste was not being segregated and disposed of according to IPC guidelines. Staff showed poor knowledge about safe medical waste handling. The private contractor responsible for collecting and disposing of medical waste had also not received proper training."The hospital's infection-control failures persisted despite the establishment of an Infection Prevention and Control Committee. The commission also cited staff unionisation and a lack of cooperation with safety protocols as factors that had compromised the handling of medical waste.Following independent inquiries, Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah ordered the suspension of 37 officers and officials, including administrators, laboratory personnel and nursing staff.The outbreak has renewed concerns over repeated failures in Pakistan's healthcare system. The country has faced several HIV outbreaks over the past decade, including the 2019 Ratodero outbreak, in which hundreds of children were infected. That investigation also exposed unsafe injection practices, poor sterilisation and weak oversight.The Sindh government has continued screening people in the affected area, promised treatment at public expense and announced a long-term fund for children affected by the outbreak. However, the Valika Hospital findings have raised concerns that similar infection-control failures could exist in other public and private healthcare facilities.
Article Summary: At least 78 children have contracted HIV in an outbreak in Pakistan's Karachi. The outbreak is linked to serious infection-control and medical waste management failures. Inspectors found needles manually removed from syringes, inadequate sterilisation safeguards and untrained staff handling contaminated waste.

Article Title: Pakistan's fifth province? Gilgit-Baltistan assembly passes key resolution amid PoK unrest
Article Text:
Gilgit-Baltistan (AP photo)

Is Pakistan preparing to make Gilgit-Baltistan its fifth province? Amid ongoing unrest in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, the Gilgit-Baltistan assembly has passed a resolution urging Islamabad to grant the region provisional provincial status, a move that could majorly redefine its administrative structure.The Gilgit-Baltistan assembly on Thursday passed a resolution, backed by both ruling and opposition sides, urging Islamabad to grant the region provisional provincial status, according to Dawn.The resolution, moved by lawmaker Jalal Ali Shah, also sought constitutional and political rights for the people of the mountainous region.Gilgit-Baltistan, located in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, currently has a semi-provincial administrative status.Pakistan currently has four provinces -- Punjab, Sindh, Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. If Islamabad accepts the proposal, Gilgit-Baltistan would become the country's fifth province under a provisional arrangement.
Article Summary: The Gilgit-Baltistan assembly has passed a resolution urging Islamabad to grant the region provisional provincial status. Pakistan currently has four provinces -- Punjab, Sindh, Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. If Islamabad accepts the proposal, Gilgit would become the country's fifth province under a provisional arrangement.

Article Title: 'Take off uniform and contest elections': Pakistani MP's open challenge to its military
Article Text:
Pakistani MP challenges their military ( Image quality improved using AI)

Critique on Baloch and Pashtun region

Critique of military

Petition filed against Fazl over remarks

Pakistani politician and chief of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl, Maulana Fazlur Rehman, delivered a blistering critique of Pakistan's military and government, accusing them of failing to maintain order in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan while warning that the country's Pashtun regions were "drowning in blood.""The country is falling apart. In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa today, there is no government. After the sun sets in the west, until the sun rises in the morning, the police do not step out of their stations. And if the police do not come out of their stations, then the streets will be handed over to armed groups, then the streets and roads will be at the mercy of bandits," Fazl said during a rally Punjab, Pakistan.He directly addressed the military: "I know your authority in my province — you have no government. You are just sitting inside your grand bungalows in the capitals, legs crossed, thinking you are the rulers. At the very least, in my province, you have no government."Fazl said Balochistan had already slipped out of government control and the Pashtun region was now following suit. "In Balochistan, in the Baloch areas, there were rebellions; the entire Baloch region had slipped out of Pakistan's control. Even today, there is no writ of the Pakistan government there.But we were holding back the Baloch region; now the Pashtun region too is drowning in blood."He described the human toll: "In the Pashtun region, within two or three days, we have received more than fifty bodies. All we did in the markets was buy shrouds for our loved ones. All we did was perform funerals for our loved ones."Fazl took aim at military personnel, accusing them of failing to protect citizens despite being paid from public taxes. "Your youth who are becoming martyrs — they have tied the uniform for this very reason, they are taking their salary for this very reason — that they have to fight for the country's security. What favor are you doing me by throwing your blood on me? You are taking your salary from the taxes of my blood and sweat for precisely this. "He added: "I have taken no salary; I will not form any army. You will leave, but you are pushing my homeland toward personal vendettas for generations to come, pushing it toward murder and plunder forever and ever. Explain this politics to someone else; don't try to explain it to us."Fazl challenged the military to enter politics directly. "If you want to do politics, then take off the uniform and come; participate in the elections, and it will become clear what votes people give to those in uniform. It is your prerogative to give government to whomever you want, and to snatch it away from whomever you wish."A petition was filed in a court against Fazl over his remarks, with the petitioner arguing that the speech hurt the sentiments of the general public and caused distress to the families of martyrs. The court sought a reply from the National Counter Terrorism Authority by August 17.Pakistani defence minister Khawaja Asif expressed disappointment, calling Fazl's words "unfair." Pakistan’s planning minister Ahsan Iqbal posted on X: "To describe such an unparalleled sacrifice as merely a compensation for a salary is neither fair, nor in accordance with the demands of ethics, and nor aligned with Islamic teachings."
Article Summary: Pakistani politician Maulana Fazlur Rehman delivered a blistering critique of Pakistan's military and government. He accused them of failing to maintain order in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan. He warned that the country's Pashtun regions were "drowning in blood"

Article Title: 'Extreme brutality': Pakistan's PTI to launch nationwide protests for Imran Khan's release
Article Text:
.

The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf parliamentary party has decided to launch a nationwide movement from August 5 for the release of party chief Imran Khan and acceptance of other demands, a day that will mark the completion of the former prime minister's third year in prison.The decision was made at a meeting chaired by party's interim chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan at Khyber Pakhtunkhwa House in Islamabad, where PTI lawmakers discussed parliamentary affairs and the party's strategy going forward.PTI General Secretary Salman Akram Raja told Dawn that the movement would include public meetings, demonstrations and a long march. "It was also decided that Mehmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas's opinions will be sought for finalising the protest plans and other activities," he said.At a press conference, Gohar said the meeting discussed the health of Imran Khan and his spouse Bushra Bibi. He said August 5 would mark the completion of three years of the PTI founder's imprisonment and rallies would be held across the country to mark the occasion.Khan was arrested on August 5, 2023 after an Islamabad trial court found him guilty of corrupt practices in the Tosha Khana case. He has since been convicted in several cases and remains in solitary confinement at Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi.Raja alleged that Khan had been kept in solitary confinement for months and that no one from his family or lawyers had been allowed to meet him since December last year. "He is not given proper medical care nor is he getting justice from the courts. The oppression and injustice in the country must come to an end," he said.He also warned the government not to launch a crackdown against party workers."Extreme brutality is being carried out here. Imran Khan is being denied meetings with his lawyers, while his sisters are also being barred from seeing him," Raja said as he sat surrounded by party workers outside the jail.Every week, Khan's sisters, lawyers and party workers gather outside Adiala Jail to press the government to allow the family to meet him. On June 14, Khan was taken to a hospital in Islamabad for treatment of his ailing right eye and later shifted back to prison.In a separate development, PTI lawyer Awais Younas Chaudhry submitted a list of six leaders to the Adiala jail administration for a meeting with Imran Khan. The list includes Haji Amanullah Awan, Muhammad Shahid Ali Chahan, Syed Hamid Ihsan, Sajjad Ali Butt, Noman Mughal and Aqsa Hayyat Lali.
Article Summary: The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf parliamentary party has decided to launch a nationwide movement from August 5. The decision was made at a meeting chaired by party's interim chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan. Khan was arrested on August 5, 2023 after an Islamabad trial court found him guilty of corrupt practices. He has since been convicted in several cases and remains in solitary confinement at Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi.
